reason: Functional: an icon-only button that opens the search area. The label names the action and the scope, and there is no visible text on the button for it to contradict.

Functional: the navigation menu button. The SVG title says "Menu", but it sits inside an aria-hidden span, so the only thing announced is the button's own label, which names the action. No competing reference.
Functional: the logo links to the site root. The alt is the brand name plus "logo", describing the image rather than the destination, even though the link's title attribute says "Home".

Functional: a card linking to the Pro Git book. The book glyph carries an empty alt and is aria-hidden because the heading beside it says "Pro Git Book", which is the redundancy filter applied correctly.
Functional: the masthead links to the site's own root. The alt is the bare publication name, so a person hears the brand but not that the link goes home.
Functional: opens the quick links menu. The button already displays "Quick Links" and the aria-label only repeats it in lower case, so nothing was written for the chevron itself.
Functional: a link to the sign-in page. The link's own text carries the label and the person icon has no alternative text of its own.
Functional: the mobile header logo links to the site root. The alt is the agency name plus "Logo", which names the image instead of the destination.
Functional, and reading mechanics rather than navigation: an arrow that returns the reader to the top of the document, so the sub-type is a reader control. The alt names exactly what it does.
Functional: the site logo links to the documentation root. The alt transcribes the wordmark, which is the brand name, and says nothing about the link going home.

A magazine cover inside a subscribe link, so a content image rather than a functional graphic. The announced name joins the hidden word "Subscribe" to the issue date, which describes the cover instead of the action.

Functional: an icon-only button that opens the search area. The label names the action and what appears, and differs from fi-2181's wording on the same site, which is a real variation rather than a duplicate.
Functional: an icon-only search button. The label names the action, and the SVG title agrees with it, so there is one reference and not two.

Functional: the logo links to the site root and the announced name is "home", which is the destination and nothing else. The same site ships "SourceForge logo" on the other template, so this pair is instructive.
A YouTube thumbnail inside a carousel tab, so a content image rather than a functional graphic. The tab is labelled only by position, "Slide 1", which tells a person nothing about what it will show.
Functional: a card linking to the videos page. The video glyph is aria-hidden with an empty alt because the heading beside it reads "Videos". Same template as fi-1705 and the same correct decision.

A magazine cover in a subscribe link, and the alt is production metadata: "Poetry June2026 cover CMYK" names a colour space and the wrong month. That is asset bookkeeping, not information for a reader.
Functional: the wordmark links to the site's own home page. Both the link label and the SVG title are the bare publication name, which does not name the destination.
Functional: opens the quick links menu. The button displays "Quick Links" and the label only adds the word "Open", so the chevron itself has no alternative text.
Same finding as fi-4890: a video thumbnail inside a carousel tab labelled only "Slide 2", which is a position rather than a description of anything.
Functional: the logo on the mailing list site links to the project's main site, a different host, so the brand name is the destination here rather than a bare name on the current site's own root.
The alt is the single word "Logo", which conveys nothing, and the href is a bare fragment that goes nowhere. Both halves of the control are broken.
Not functional: a decorative illustration on an onboarding card, not a glyph standing for a function. Its empty alt is correct, because the card's own heading and description carry the label.
Functional: opens the catalogue mega menu. The button already displays "Explore" and the label extends that text, so the chevron beside it has no alternative text of its own.

Functional: the logo links to the site root, and the announced "Al Jazeera , link to home page" is genuinely good text. But it comes from hidden text beside the logo, and the figure holding the SVG is aria-hidden, so the graphic itself has no description.
Same finding as fi-4890 and fi-4891, on a different page: a video thumbnail in a carousel tab labelled only by its position.
Functional: the brand link goes to the documentation root. The alt describes the elephant artwork and ends in "Logo", which is the visual detail the criteria call irrelevant.
Not functional: a decorative calendar illustration on an onboarding card. The empty alt is correct because the card's heading and description carry the label. Same finding as fi-10185.
Functional: the logo links to the same site's root. The alt is the bare project name, with nothing to say the link goes home.
Functional: the submit button of the search form, so a form control rather than a toggle. The icon-only button is labelled with the action it performs.
